GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2021-03-18T21:48:33Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Distributed Tables missing records. "Exception: Too large string size." in logs.
Description: Setup:
```
         <shard>
              <weight>1</weight>
              <internal_replication>false</internal_replication>
              <replica>
                  <host><server1domainname></host>
                  <port>9000</port>
              </replica>
              <replica>
                  <host><server2domainname></host>
                  <port>9000</port>
              </replica>
          </shard>

```
Our code writes to a Distributed table on either server, and then clickhouse writes the record to the underlying real tables on both servers. 

No zookeeper.

This has been working for a few years.

Incident.
To get multivolume support, I upgraded from 18.14.19 to 20.8.12.2. I had a number of problems, and ran out of time to debug/fix, so I rolled back to 18.14.19. My problem probably started then.

Now we have discovered that some records are not getting replicated to one of the servers. Or maybe replication is working from server1 -> server2, but not the other way. I'm not 100% sure. When reads randomly choose a server, they get different results.

I have these error messages constantly on one server:

`2021.03.19 02:35:13.294443 [ 39 ] {} <Error> <table>.Distributed.DirectoryMonitor: Poco::Exception. Code: 1000, e.code() = 0, e.displayText() = Exception: Too large string size., e.what() = Exception
`

I also noticed a small number of these errors on the other server, but they are not constant. Only a handful from a few hours ago.

`2021.03.18 19:22:36.647630 [ 38 ] {} <Error> <table>.Distributed.DirectoryMonitor: Code: 252, e.displayText() = DB::Exception: Received from <serverdomainname>:9000, <ipaddress> DB::Exception: Too many parts (304). Merges are processing significantly slower than inserts..
`

I did some research into the first error, but I don't really understand which directory, or which string it is referring to.

Thanks.
